name: Moffitt Cancer Center: Neuro-Oncology
focus: Brain and spinal cord tumors; multidisciplinary tumor assessment.
why_relevant: A route for a tumor-focused second opinion. Ask specifically for assessment of neurological deficits and coordination with rehabilitation.
search_terms: brain tumor diagnosis second opinion movement hand weakness sensation numbness gait balance
caution: Confirm tumor type, age eligibility and referral requirements. A tumor consultation is different from a dedicated hand-function assessment.

name: Froedtert & Medical College of Wisconsin: Tumor Rehabilitation
focus: Rehabilitation after brain and spine tumor treatment.
why_relevant: The program describes physical and occupational therapy for tumor-related functional difficulties, including weakness and spasticity.
search_terms: brain tumor hand arm weakness spasticity clenching clenched numbness hemiplegia coordination rehab occupational therapy balance walking
caution: Ask which clinic assesses upper-limb tone and hand use, and whether a separate movement-disorders consultation is appropriate.

name: Shirley Ryan AbilityLab: Spasticity Management
focus: Spasticity, muscle tightness, contracture and functional rehabilitation.
why_relevant: A problem-focused service for evaluating muscle overactivity and its effect on function. Includes adult and pediatric services.
search_terms: spasticity dystonia clenched clenching hand arm brain tumor trauma brain injury spinal cord injury rehab occupational therapy contracture gait walking
caution: Its page describes neurological conditions broadly, not a tumor-specific pathway. Confirm acceptance of the particular diagnosis and age. Matching here does not establish that clenching is spasticity.

name: Mayo Clinic: Brachial Plexus Team
focus: Multidisciplinary assessment and reconstruction of brachial plexus injuries.
why_relevant: Relevant when arm loss after trauma is attributed to the brachial plexus or needs specialist localization. The team describes care from infancy through adulthood.
search_terms: accident trauma arm hand brachial plexus nerve injury avulsion paralysis weakness nerve transfer nerve graft muscle transfer repair EMG
caution: An accident can also injure the brain or spinal cord. Confirm the injury site; some nerve reconstruction decisions are time-sensitive.

name: Johns Hopkins: Neuro-Ophthalmology / Neuro-Visual Clinic
focus: Neurological causes of abnormal eye movements, double vision and other visual symptoms.
why_relevant: A specialist assessment route for eye movement or alignment problems alongside neurological symptoms.
search_terms: eye vision alignment deviation outward eye double vision brain tumor numbness balance gait
caution: The page describes neuro-visual disorders generally. Confirm age acceptance and suitability for the specific tumor history; a visible eye change alone does not identify its cause.

name: Johns Hopkins All Children’s: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine
why_relevant: A pediatric rehabilitation entry point for assessment of function and muscle tone, with related specialty services.
search_terms: child pediatric hand clenching clenched spasticity dystonia weakness rehab brain injury brain tumor arm gait occupational therapy
caution: This is a general pediatric rehabilitation service, not a confirmed tumor-specific hand clinic. Ask about diagnosis eligibility and age limits.

name: Nicholas A. Pulos, MD: Mayo Clinic
focus: Hand and microvascular surgery, including traumatic and birth-related brachial plexus injuries.
why_relevant: An official specialist profile to explore if a brachial plexus or peripheral nerve injury has been identified.
search_terms: brachial plexus peripheral nerve trauma accident hand arm nerve transfer reconstruction surgery
caution: Listed for documented clinical focus, not as a ranked best doctor. Confirm current availability, age eligibility and the appropriate team before travel.

name: Columbia University: Postoperative Motor Recovery Study
focus: Pilot rTMS study after surgical removal of a brain tumor, NCT07530536.
why_relevant: A research contact for postoperative movement deficits. The registry lists recruiting; the site must confirm current openings and eligibility.
search_terms: brain tumor hand weakness motor movement rehab magnetic stimulation TMS clinical trial surgery
caution: Ages 22–65; surgical resection required; chronic deficits must be within three years of surgery. Any clinical seizure history is excluded. Not established treatment and not an eligibility determination.

name: Brooks Rehabilitation: Brain Tumor Rehabilitation
location: Jacksonville and other Florida locations, USA
focus: Rehabilitation for brain tumor related movement, coordination, daily-living and cognitive difficulties before, during or after treatment.
why_relevant: The program explicitly describes brain tumor rehabilitation with physical, occupational and speech therapy, plus balance and vestibular services. A cancer rehabilitation navigator helps coordinate with cancer care providers.
search_terms: brain tumor meningioma hand arm weakness motor coordination rehab occupational therapy gait balance walking
caution: Confirm age eligibility, the appropriate location, referral and insurance requirements, and availability of a hand-function or spasticity assessment. The program page does not confirm that every site offers every service. A listing is not confirmation of acceptance or treatment benefit.

name: Kennedy Krieger Institute: IMPACT cerebellar rehabilitation study
focus: Research screening for personalized tDCS plus rehabilitation for cerebellar damage; participants choose hand dexterity/arm control, walking/balance, or speech therapy.
why_relevant: The registry explicitly includes tumor-related cerebellar damage and a hand/arm therapy track. This is a study-specific assessment route for adults aged 18–75, not a general diagnosis or routine-care referral service.
search_terms: brain tumor cerebellar ataxia hand dexterity arm control coordination gait walking balance rehabilitation stimulation tDCS IMPACT NCT07642856
caution: Recruiting according to registry and listed Baltimore site, checked 2026-10-24; sponsor last verified status June 2026 and last update posted 2026-06-11. No results posted. Ages 18–75; children are not eligible. Excludes seizure history, specified medications, MRI safety/tolerance problems, task-interfering impairments and conditions preventing safe exercise; see full criteria. No explicit tumor-treatment or symptom-onset window is listed, so confirm directly. Protocol describes MRI-response/tolerability screening and has inconsistent masking descriptions. Listing does not confirm current openings, acceptance of any tumor type, or suitability for unexplained clenching, sensory loss or peripheral-nerve injury. Contact details are published for research inquiries, not emergencies, and were not tested.

name: UW Medical Center - Montlake: Rehabilitation Medicine Clinic
focus: Rehabilitation assessment for cancer-related neurological disability, brain injury, spinal cord injury and movement problems.
why_relevant: The clinic explicitly includes neuro-oncology and evaluation for occupational and physical therapy. UW also lists spasticity management; clinic physiatrist Ny-Ying Lam's official profile confirms neurorehabilitation and spasticity interests.
search_terms: brain tumor hand arm weakness clenching clenched spasticity tone sensation numbness coordination grasp release gait balance walking rehabilitation occupational therapy trauma brain injury spinal cord injury
caution: A general assessment route, not a confirmed tumor-specific hand clinic or acceptance of any individual diagnosis. Confirm age eligibility, referral requirements, appropriate clinician and availability. Clenching does not establish spasticity or dystonia. After an accident, confirm whether the injury involves brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerves; this listing does not establish the injury site. Published phone was not tested; no provider was contacted.

name: Unity Health Toronto: EASE Pain MDMA trial
focus: Screening for MDMA-assisted therapy research in severe chronic neuropathic pain, NCT07301632.
why_relevant: The registry explicitly includes clinician-confirmed neuropathic pain lasting over three months despite inadequate benefit from at least two recommended medications. It is a research screening route, not a general hand rehabilitation service.
search_terms: MDMA EASEPain EASE Pain neuropathic nerve pain chronic severe trial Toronto Akash Goel
caution: Recruiting in registry and Toronto site, checked 2026-10-25; last update posted 2026-07-29, sponsor status-verification field October 2025. Adults 18 or older; specified pain thresholds and extensive medical/medication exclusions apply, including seizure disorders, prior MDMA use and current SSRI/SNRI treatment. No results posted. Does not establish nerve regrowth, hand-motor recovery, tumor eligibility or acceptance. Openings, travel requirements and individual eligibility must be confirmed. Do not alter medicines to qualify. Public contact details were not tested; no provider was contacted.
